root.name: Latvian Gambit: Fraser Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Nc6

overview: After 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f5 3.Nxe5 Nc6, Black counters the usual 3...Qf6 by attacking the knight, and White usually takes 4.Nxc6 dxc6 with a lead in development for Black a pawn down, followed by d3 or d4. The sound line for White is to return the pawn only when safe and consolidate. It is a trappy, rarely seen branch of the Latvian.

white_ideas.idea: Take on c6 and play d3/d4 with a solid extra pawn
Develop quickly and keep the king safe on the e1-h4 diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Use the bishop pair and open d-file for activity

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White a pawn up after Nxc6 dxc6
Black pawn on f5 and open e-file

character.notes: Black plays for tactics and gambit pawns; White is better if safe, but traps abound.

gambit.notes: Black loses the e-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: The Latvian is considered refuted or close to it by theory.

structure.notes: Centre opens with exchanges on c6 and e4.

approach.notes: The Latvian is one of the anchors for Offbeat.

level.notes: Dubious lines are not recommended; it needs surprise more than understanding.

plan_phrases: black gambit for lead in development

sublines_that_differ.name: Nxc6 main line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Nc6 4. Nxc6 dxc6
sublines_that_differ.how: The usual practical choice with a clear plus for White.

character.reason: Black gambits and White must avoid traps around f5, e4 and the king.

gambit.reason: Black loses a pawn on e5 which White can keep.

soundness.reason: The Latvian is considered close to refuted.

structure.reason: Open e- and d-files after exchanges.

approach.reason: Latvian Gambit is an Offbeat anchor.

level.reason: Dubious so never Beginner; traps need to be memorised.

plans.reason: Black seeks quick development for the pawn.
